# Fixture projects

Small repositories with `.virgil-lsp.json` project files ([format](../../../docs/configuration.md)). Each directory is one repository root.

| Directory | Projects | What it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `two-programs/` | `server`, `client` | Two programs that share `shared/Greeting.v3` and both declare a top-level `Program`. Each program verifies alone, but analyzing all three files as one program reports `TypeRedefined`. |
| `two-file/` | `shapes` | Copies of `test/fixtures/analysis/two-file` as a project: `main.v3` uses `Shapes` and `Rect` from the tab-indented `shapes.v3`. The [semantic diagnostic transcripts](../../diagnostics/run.py) edit them in unsaved buffers. |
| `compiler-flags/` | `descriptors`, `read-only`, `defaults` | Projects with different `compilerArgs`. `descriptors/Described.v3` parses only with `-lang:descriptors`. `read-only` and `defaults` share `shared/Table.v3`, which uses `array<int>`: it verifies only with `-lang:read-only-arrays`, which only `read-only` sets. The [compiler-flags transcript](../../diagnostics/compiler-flags.jsonl) and `LspProjectAnalysisTest.v3` use it. |
| `virgil-lib/` | `words` | A program that uses Virgil's `lib/util` through `virgilDependencies`, which are relative to the Virgil root. It verifies only with `lib/util/*.v3`. |

`prepare.py <build-directory>` creates additional filesystem cases under the build directory, rather than storing special files in Git: a sparse source larger than 4 MiB, a FIFO, a socket, file/directory symlinks, a symlink cycle, and projects at aggregate source-reference and path-byte limits. It also records the repository root for tests that use the checked-in fixtures, independently of executable placement. The unit-test build runs this script on both CI hosts. Two fixture directories under `<build-directory>/project-fixtures`, `unreadable-directories/blocked` and `ignored-entries/build`, are created with mode `0700` (owner read, write, and execute); `prepare.py <build-directory> --restrict` sets them to `000`, `--cleanup` restores `0700`, and `--run COMMAND [ARGUMENT ...]` does both around the command. The wrapper restores permissions after a pass, a failure, SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP, preserving the command's exit status or returning 128 plus the signal number. `make test` and `make test-unit` use `test/unit/run.py` through the `run-unit-tests` target; the [development guide](../../../docs/development.md#tests) describes group scheduling and output behavior. With patterns the runner uses `--run`; otherwise it applies `--restrict` and `--cleanup` in every slot. The first slot is `<build-directory>` itself; extra slots are `<build-directory>/unit-slots/<n>` and have their own generated fixtures and copies of the unit-test executable and both worker builds, each with a distinct inode so executable-path discovery stays within its slot on every platform. Before probing the test count, the grouped runner restores permissions and removes extra slots left by an interrupted run. After this run, it restores fixture permissions in every slot and removes its extra slots, so the build directory stays removable; `test_cleanup.py` drives that target with a stand-in executable and a pattern to check the wrapping itself, and `test/unit/test_run.py` checks the run of each group, termination included. `ProjectExpansionTest.v3` tests enumeration, UTF-8 glob semantics, deterministic ordering, exclusions, library bases, source admission, the canonical URIs that selected sources keep, capacity transfer during preflight, and the no-symlink policy. `LspProjectAnalysisTest.v3` uses `two-programs` to test separate snapshots and configuration changes during pending analyses.
